# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 25 (Bu-Vb Np25)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Np25
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 25
**Title (English, from literature):** Taking back robe-cloth in anger
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cīvaraacchindana Sutta* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 25) is a Vinaya text belonging to the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga. The rule addresses the case of a Buddhist monk who gives robe-cloth to a fellow monk and subsequently reclaims it out of anger; committing this infraction entails forfeiture (*nissaggiya*) of the robe-cloth and formal confession (*pācittiya*) of the offense. An English translation of the rule and its commentary has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Within the Pali tradition, it corresponds directly to Bhikkhu Pātimokkha Nissaggiya Pācittiya 25, Bhikkhu Parivāra Nissaggiya Pācittiya 25, and parallel nuns' rules in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (Bi-Vb Np26) and Bhikkhunī Parivāra. Close Vinaya parallels exist in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions across diverse monastic schools, including the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya Vinayas, as well as the *Upāliparipṛcchā*.
